scope_note: Second corrective modeled-synthesis gate under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Fifteen bounded syntheses survive: nine exact Winner-only annual paid-property-tax aggregations for 2017-2025, the 2025 same-scope marginal-service-cost break-even identity, one deterministic 2018 gross-before-realized-abatement counterfactual, one low-confidence 2020 operating-payroll sensitivity, and three 2024 resource syntheses for EIA benchmark electricity cost, deterministic leap-year average load, and EPA eGRID ERCT/Texas location-factor emissions. MMI Southwest is excluded from every Winner aggregation. None is a new source observation, selected-building allocation, audited recipient receipt, actual payroll, utility bill, peak demand, actual or market-based emissions, observed public cost, or net fiscal result. County outcome, construction, supplier, induced, actual-bill, market-based-emissions and net-fiscal models remain rejected.

sources.title: Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington, TX — May 2020 Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates
sources.notes: Official all-industry metropolitan table reports annual mean wages of $56,190 for all occupations, $97,540 for computer and mathematical occupations, and $162,180 for computer and information systems managers. BLS identifies Tarrant County within the Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington area and annualizes hourly means using 2,080 hours. These are scenario anchors, not Meta wages, benefits, occupation mix or payroll.

sources.title: Electric Power Annual 2024 — Table 2.10, average electricity price by state and sector
sources.notes: Final EIA-861 table reports Texas average retail electricity prices of 6.12 cents/kWh industrial and 8.55 cents/kWh commercial for 2024, and 6.60 cents/kWh industrial for 2023. EIA notes that commercial/industrial classification can depend on NAICS or demand/usage rate schedules. These statewide averages are benchmarks, not Meta's retailer contract, Oncor delivery tariff or bill.

sources.title: Oncor Tariff for Retail Delivery Service
sources.notes: The current PUCT-approved delivery tariff lists Tarrant County in Oncor's certified service area and shows distinct primary-distribution, primary-substation and transmission-service schedules with customer, metering, demand and rider charges. It establishes why kWh alone cannot reconstruct Meta's historical delivery or total bill; the current tariff is not used as a 2024 price.

sources.title: Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act — customer choice, metering and billing provisions
sources.notes: PURA separates the retail electric provider from the transmission and distribution utility in customer-choice areas and provides that the utility bills nonbypassable delivery charges to the retail provider. Meta's provider, contract price, rate class and meter determinants are not public, preventing an actual-bill estimate.

sources.title: ERCOT Organization Backgrounder
sources.notes: ERCOT identifies Fort Worth as an urban load center within its region and describes its competitive wholesale and retail-switching roles. This supports ERCT regional context but does not identify Meta's retail provider, nodal price, tariff, contract, load shape or emissions attributes.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Summary Tables, Revision 2
sources.notes: EPA reports 2023 total-output CO2e rates of 736.629 lb/MWh for ERCT/ERCOT All and 771.2 lb/MWh for Texas generation. The model uses them as alternative geographic location-based factors without grid-loss uplift, marginal/non-baseload substitution, avoided-emissions credit or renewable-contract adjustment.

estimates.label: 2025 Winner-account local service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: Tax year 2025 equal-cost threshold for the same four Winner paid-tax components

scope.label: Winner LLC real account 42324937 and personal account 14401610 at 4500 Like Way across five Tarrant-serviced units and Northwest ISD

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the same-scope 2025 paid-tax aggregation by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public cost.

estimates.confidence_rationale: The identity and tax inputs are exact, while actual same-scope marginal public costs and recipient cash reconciliation are unavailable.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the public-cost level that would exactly offset the latest Winner paid-tax base without fabricating a service cost or fiscal surplus.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Annual marginal fire, police, road, water, wastewater, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs aligned to the same accounts, recipients and tax year

derivation.formula: annual same-scope marginal public-service cost at break-even = $6,857,574.58 + $7,536,463.62 + $16,456,685.62 + $18,162,864.32 = $49,013,588.14
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed or estimated public cost.
Its account, recipient and tax-year scope matches the 2025 paid-tax aggregation.
MMI, incentives, public financing and utility costs are excluded.
No positive or negative fiscal margin is asserted.

limitations: Actual same-scope marginal public cost is unobserved.
Recipient costs may differ across the six taxing units.
The threshold is unallocated to the selected building.
estimates.notes: Do not sum this threshold with the tax contribution or report it as cost, net benefit or fiscal surplus.

parameters.name: reported_people_floor

provenance.detail: Operator says more than 150 people worked at the data center on December 8, 2020

May 2020 Dallas-Fort Worth computer and mathematical annual mean wage

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Exact direct/contract FTE, annual hours and persistence, occupation mix, cash wages, benefits, payroll taxes, bonus/equity, overtime, contractor margin, residence and selected-building allocation

estimates.notes: Do not combine with the 200-plus jobs-supported projection or report as actual payroll, benefits, local labor income or an employment effect.

derivation.formula: 1,109,004 MWh × total-output lb CO2e/MWh ÷ 2,204.62262185 lb/metric ton
assumptions: ERCT is the central consumption-region factor because ERCOT identifies Fort Worth inside its region; Texas state output is an alternative production-geography sensitivity.
